# Study file format

A study is one JSON file, `NAME.aikidoe.json`: the factors and responses, the design with its
run order, every observation, the measurement structure and the history of stages. It is the
record of the experiment; the app and `doe` read and write the same file. Comments (`//`,
`/* */`) and trailing commas are allowed.

An aikidoe study file (*.aikidoe.json), format version 1: factors, responses, constraints, the design and its run order, observations, drop-in sites, the stage history and an optional simulator. Comments and trailing commas are allowed in the file (JSON with comments); this schema describes the JSON value.

The format is published as a JSON Schema: [schema/study.schema.json](../../schema/study.schema.json)
(`doe schema` prints it). The schema checks the structure;
the library checks the rest when it reads a study:

> Rules a JSON Schema cannot express, checked by the library's validateStudy: high > low; factor and response ids all distinct; a log-transformed factor has low > 0 and positive settings; every run's settings give every factor and nothing else, with a categorical value among its levels; run and order numbers are distinct; runs in one whole plot share their hard-to-change settings; observations refer to runs in the design and to non-derived responses; derived.from names a non-derived response; history runs are in the design; constraints are linear in continuous factor ids; mixture components are continuous factors (not log, not hard to change) with low ≥ 0, their lows add up to less than the total and their highs to at least it, and every run's components add up to the total; a count response's values are whole numbers ≥ 0, a binomial response's successes lie between 0 and the trials (the response's or the observation's), a bernoulli response's are 0 or 1, and exposure is only for counts with the log link; a target lies between lower and upper; goal 'target' needs a target and goal 'range' lower and upper.

## Top level

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `aikidoe` (required) | `1` | study format version |
| `name` | string | a short title |
| `description` | string | what the study is for |
| `seed` (required) | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 4294967295) | seed of every random step (randomisation, searches) |
| `factors` (required) | list of [factor](#factor) (at least 1) | the factors varied (continuous or categorical) |
| `responses` | list of [response](#response) | what is measured |
| `covariates` | list of [covariate](#covariate) | covariates: variables that are measured but not set (a starting weight, the room temperature), with their values; models take them as terms by id (issue #82) |
| `constraints` | list of [constraint](#constraint) | linear constraints on the settings |
| `design` | [design](#design) | the runs, in standard order, with their randomised run order |
| `observations` | list of [observation](#observation) | results: one per reading (run, response, and wafer / site / repeat when measured that way) |
| `sites` | [sites](#sites) | drop-in measurement sites on the wafer |
| `plates` | [plates](#plates) | microplate layout: each run in a well, controls on every plate |
| `mixture` | [mixture](#mixture) | mixture components: factors that are shares of a whole, adding up to the total (issue #62) |
| `history` | list of [stage](#stage) | the stages of a sequential experiment |
| `simulator` | object | the simulator that runs the design (computer experiments): { adapter, …its options } |
| `exercise` | object | an exercise this study answers (made by the exercise generator): its id, topic, difficulty, budget, questions, the sealed truth for self-study, and the student's answers |

## factor

A factor is [continuous](#continuous) or [categorical](#categorical).

## id

an identifier: letters, digits and _, not starting with a digit (`^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$`).

## label

a non-empty string or a number.

## continuous

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | [id](#id) | used in formulas, constraints and run sheets |
| `name` | string | a readable name |
| `units` | string | shown in tables and run sheets |
| `type` | `"continuous"` | optional: inferred from levels |
| `low` | number | the low end of the range (coded −1) |
| `high` | number | the high end of the range (coded +1) |
| `levels` | list of number (at least 2) | the levels a multi-level design uses (sorted) |
| `transform` | `"none"` \| `"log"` | log: coded on the log scale (e.g. time, dose) |
| `htc` | boolean | hard to change: split-plot designs |
| `tolerance` | number (≥ 0) or object | standard deviation of the actual value about its setting (natural units), or a distribution |
| `noise` | object | a noise factor: varied in the experiment, random in production: { sd, mean? } (natural units) |
| `note` | string | free text |

Give `low` and `high`, or `levels` (then the range is their extent).

## categorical

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | [id](#id) |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `units` | string |  |
| `type` | `"categorical"` | optional when a level is a string |
| `levels` (required) | list of [label](#label) (at least 2) | two or more distinct levels |
| `htc` | boolean | hard to change: split-plot designs |
| `note` | string |  |

Without `type`, a factor whose levels include a string is categorical.

## response

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | [id](#id) |  |
| `name` | string |  |
| `units` | string |  |
| `distribution` | `"normal"` \| `"poisson"` \| `"quasipoisson"` \| `"negbin"` \| `"binomial"` \| `"quasibinomial"` \| `"bernoulli"` | the kind of value and its noise (issue #64): a measurement (normal), a count (poisson; negbin or quasipoisson when overdispersed), successes out of trials (binomial, quasibinomial), or pass/fail (bernoulli, 0 or 1). Anything but normal is fitted by a generalised linear model, one observation per run |
| `link` | `"identity"` \| `"log"` \| `"sqrt"` \| `"logit"` \| `"probit"` \| `"cloglog"` | the scale the model is linear on: log (default), identity or sqrt for counts; logit (default), probit or cloglog for proportions |
| `trials` | integer (≥ 1) | binomial: the number of trials in every run (otherwise each observation gives its own) |
| `goal` | `"none"` \| `"maximize"` \| `"minimize"` \| `"target"` \| `"range"` | for optimisation (desirability) |
| `target` | number | desirability target |
| `lower` | number | desirability lower limit |
| `upper` | number | desirability upper limit |
| `weight` | number (> 0) or list of any (at least 2) | desirability shape: one number, or two (below, above a target) |
| `importance` | number (> 0) | relative importance in the overall desirability |
| `levels` | list of `"lot"` \| `"run"` \| `"wholePlot"` \| `"wafer"` \| `"site"` (at least 1) | measurement hierarchy, in nesting order |
| `derived` | object | a per-wafer summary of another response, computed from its readings |
| `measurement` | object | the measurement system, from a gauge R&R study: { sigma, … } |
| `spec` | object | specification limits for yield |
| `note` | string | free text |

## design

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `kind` | string | the kind of design (fractional-factorial, ccd, split-plot-fraction, sequential, …) |
| `params` | object | the design's parameters (generators, resolution, α, …) |
| `randomisation` | `"complete"` \| `"restricted"` \| `"blocked"` \| `"none"` | complete; restricted (split-plot); blocked; or none |
| `blocking` | list of [blocking](#blocking) | named blocking variables, when the runs are grouped two or more ways (a Latin square's rows and columns, a crossover's subjects and periods); each run gives its label for each in blocks |
| `carryover` | boolean | a crossover design: the analysis adds a carry-over term (the treatment each subject had in the period before) |
| `runs` (required) | list of [run](#run) |  |

## run

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `run` (required) | integer (≥ 1) | run number (standard order) |
| `order` | integer (≥ 1) | the randomised order in which to run it |
| `wholePlot` | [label](#label) | whole plot (split-plot designs) |
| `block` | [label](#label) | block (stage, day, batch) |
| `blocks` | object | the run's label for each of design.blocking |
| `kind` | `"factorial"` \| `"fraction"` \| `"axial"` \| `"centre"` \| `"confirm"` \| `"augment"` \| `"optimal"` \| `"space-filling"` \| `"other"` | the part of the design it comes from |
| `settings` (required) | object | factor id → setting (natural units, or a level) |

## observation

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `run` (required) | integer | the run |
| `response` (required) | string | the response id |
| `value` (required) | number or null | null: missing (measured but failed) |
| `trials` | integer (≥ 1) | binomial response: the trials of this run (value is the number of successes) |
| `exposure` | number (> 0) | count response with the log link: what the count is out of (volume plated, area, cells examined); its log is an offset, so the model is for the rate (default 1) |
| `lot` | [label](#label) | lot |
| `wafer` | [label](#label) | wafer within the run |
| `site` | [label](#label) | site on the wafer |
| `slot` | [label](#label) | boat slot |
| `operator` | [label](#label) | operator |
| `repeat` | integer | repeat reading |
| `note` | string | free text |

## sites

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `scheme` | string | 5-site, 9-site, dropin-9 or custom |
| `diameter` | number (> 0) | wafer diameter, mm |
| `positions` (required) | list of object | site id and x, y in mm from the wafer centre |

## stage

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `stage` (required) | string | name: screen, foldover, axial, augment, confirm, … |
| `runs` | list of integer | the runs added in this stage |
| `date` | string | when |
| `note` | string |  |
| `params` | object | the stage's parameters |

## plates

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `rows` (required) | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 32) | rows of wells (8 for a 96-well plate) |
| `cols` (required) | integer (≥ 1, ≤ 48) | columns of wells (12 for a 96-well plate) |
| `exclude` | list of `"edge"` or string (matching `^[A-Za-z]{1,2}0*[1-9][0-9]*$`) | wells left empty: "edge" (the outer ring) or well ids |
| `controls` | list of object | control wells on every plate |
| `layout` | `"balanced"` \| `"random"` \| `"ordered"` | how the runs were placed (default balanced) |
| `seed` | integer (≥ 0, ≤ 4294967295) |  |
| `efficiency` | number | layout efficiency for the design's model (1 = position costs nothing) |
| `wells` | list of object or object | each used well: a run of the design or a control |
| `readings` | list of object | results of the control wells |

## mixture

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `components` (required) | list of [id](#id) (at least 2) | ids of continuous factors (not log, not hard to change, low ≥ 0) that are components of the mixture |
| `total` | number (> 0) | what the components add up to in every run (1, 100 %, or the batch size) |

## covariate

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | [id](#id) | used in formulas; differs from every factor and response id |
| `name` | string | display name (default: the id) |
| `units` | string |  |
| `note` | string | free text |
| `values` | list of object | the values measured: one per run, or one per wafer (lot, site) of a run when it was measured there. A run with no value is left out of a model that has the covariate |

## blocking

| field | type | |
|---|---|---|
| `id` (required) | [id](#id) | used in run sheets and for --random |
| `name` | string | a readable name (Day, Operator) |
| `role` | `"row"` \| `"column"` \| `"subject"` \| `"period"` | rows and columns of a Latin square; subjects and periods of a crossover |
| `levels` | list of [label](#label) | the labels in order (a crossover's periods in time order) |

## constraint

a linear constraint, e.g. "T + 2*t <= 1050": a string, or `{ "expr": …, "units": "natural" | "coded" }`.

## A minimal study

```json
{
  "aikidoe": 1,
  "name": "Etch rate",
  "seed": 12345,
  "factors": [
    { "id": "power", "low": 200, "high": 400, "units": "W" },
    { "id": "gas", "levels": ["CF4", "C2F6"] }
  ],
  "responses": [{ "id": "rate", "units": "nm/min" }]
}
```
